title: Savoy Church of Christ rebuilding plans; volunteer fire department formation
text:

There were 29 men who signed up as charter members of the truckless volunteer fire department. The goal is 50. A $5 membership fee per year was set up. And even as Savoy's citizens were doing something about future fires, the Church of Christ was making plans to rebuild.

The three-man board of elders, J. B. May, C. E. Corry[?] and Malcolm DeBerrry, completed their insurance settlement Monday and were told they would get $8,000 of the $8,000 carried on their building.

"We hope to start rebuilding immediately," said May. "It probably will take at least $18,000 to put up a similar building. However that undoubtedly would mean we would have to go into debt. We never have been in debt and I don't know whether we want to start now," May added.

May said it was possible that the church would see how much it could raise and then make plans to put up a building in that cost range.

With only about 39 families represented in its 100 membership, May said it would take approximately $400 per family to replace the building.

Meanwhile, services will be conducted in the Savoy high school auditorium until a new edifice is erected, the minister said.

"We met there Sunday night after the fire," the minister said, adding "and we have been given permission to hold midweek and Sunday services there."

Holligan[?], a graduate of Abilene Christian College, has been in Savoy for 16 months. He has been in the ministry for about three years. Married, he has three children.

Meanwhile, the ways and means committee had two suggested ways of raising funds for fire fighting equipment for Savoy to start with. A small bond issue was suggested and then the committee was asked to investigate the civil defense program that pays for 50 per cent of the cost so long as certain civil defense obligations are met.

And to get the volunteer firemen training started, the members will stage their first meeting Monday at Bonham when the Bonham volunteers will give them their first drill.

Savoy was supposed to have sent representatives to Monday night's meeting, but a huge blaze on the square kept the Bonham firemen at home.
notes: Article begins mid-sentence ('we easily could have'). The minister's name reads as 'Holligan[?]' — partially legible. DeBerrry spelling as in original (possible typo for DeBerrry or DeBerry). Insurance payout of $8,000 on the building. First fire drill scheduled at Bonham. The Bonham firemen were kept home by a separate fire on the square. Part of a larger 1954 fire series.
